Problem: const
Context: repo=STM32CubeF2, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=other, severity=medium, evidence_strength=medium, rescue_applied=True, state=closed, issue_number=16
Root cause: Hi @RetoFx, Thank you for the suggestion.
Fix: You add more and more const to your cube code.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, medium, enhancement, invalid, dcmi, HAL_StatusTypeDef, HAL_DCMI_ConfigSyncUnmask, DCMI_HandleTypeDef, DCMI_SyncUnmaskTypeDef

Technical details:
You add more and more const to your cube code. This is great. const is one of the most important keywords in C. For example HAL_StatusTypeDef HAL_DCMI_ConfigSyncUnmask(DCMI_HandleTypeDef *hdcmi, **const** DCMI_SyncUnmaskTypeDef *SyncUnmask); But you add const before the type. We and lot of other developer prefer, that const is after the type. This simplify the code understanding as soon as there is also a pointer. the explanation is: It helps me keep track of 'what' is constant by reading the type declaration from right to left: Type * const obj; // read right-to-left: const pointer to Object Type const * obj; // read right-to-left: pointer to const Object Type const * const obj; // read right-to-left: const pointer to const Object So please improve this asap

Key comments:
Hi @RetoFx, Thank you for the suggestion. However, as both notations, const Type * obj and Type const * obj, are the same, we prefer keeping the first one. Thank you again for your suggestion.

issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: stm32f2xx_hal_mmc.c use SDMMC_STATIC_FLAGS instead of SDIO_STATIC_FLAGS
Context: repo=STM32CubeF2, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=14
Root cause: ST Internal Reference: 186496 Fixed in commit https://github.
Fix: In file stm32f2xx_hal_mmc.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: HAL, bug_report, medium, bug, internal bug tracker, mmc, HAL_MMC_ConfigWideBusOperation, SDMMC_STATIC_FLAGS, SDIO_STATIC_FLAGS

Technical details:
In file stm32f2xx_hal_mmc.c function HAL_MMC_ConfigWideBusOperation() is SDMMC_STATIC_FLAGS used instead of SDIO_STATIC_FLAGS SDMMC_STATIC_FLAGS is defined in stm32_hal_legacy.h. But for new projects stm32_hal_legacy.h should not be used. Either you replace SDMMC_STATIC_FLAGS with SDIO_STATIC_FLAGS or you add the following code to stm32f2xx_hal_mmc.c (and similar files) #if !defined( SDMMC_STATIC_FLAGS ) #if defined( SDIO_STATIC_FLAGS ) #define SDMMC_STATIC_FLAGS SDIO_STATIC_FLAGS #endif #endif #if !defined( SDIO_STATIC_FLAGS ) #if defined( SDMMC_STATIC_FLAGS ) #define SDIO_STATIC_FLAGS SDMMC_STATIC_FLAGS #endif #endif then both symboles are defined

Key comments:
ST Internal Reference: 186496 Fixed in commit https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF2/commit/190a39c1bdbea901648ed167af4e12a45f923546

issues.issue_title: Babble error is not in HCD_HC_IN_IRQHandler
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: Babble error is not in HCD_HC_IN_IRQHandler
Context: repo=STM32CubeF2, mcu_series=None, board=STM32F4XX, component=USB, layer=HAL, issue_kind=other, severity=high, evidence_strength=medium, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=3
Root cause: Hi @froha, Thank you for your report.
Fix: The flag USB_OTG_HCINT_BBERR is not handled in the HCD_HC_IN_IRQHandler.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: STM32F4XX, HAL, USB, high, enhancement, spotted before customer, USB_OTG_HCINT_BBERR, HCD_HC_IN_IRQHandler, USBx_HC, ch_num, HCINT, HC_BBLERR

Technical details:
The flag USB_OTG_HCINT_BBERR is not handled in the HCD_HC_IN_IRQHandler. So if this occurs, then the flag would never be cleared and the interrupt is always running. The CubeF4 HCD_HC_IN_IRQHandler does handle the babble error: else if ((USBx_HC(ch_num)->HCINT & USB_OTG_HCINT_BBERR) == USB_OTG_HCINT_BBERR) { __HAL_HCD_CLEAR_HC_INT(ch_num, USB_OTG_HCINT_BBERR); hhcd->hc[ch_num].state = HC_BBLERR; __HAL_HCD_UNMASK_HALT_HC_INT(ch_num); (void)USB_HC_Halt(hhcd->Instance, (uint8_t)ch_num); }

Key comments:
Hi @froha, Thank you for your report. May I ask you the firmware version you are using and the file the potential issue is located into. Hi @ALABSTM, we use a combination from the old Standard Peripherals Library and only the USB part from the STM32CubeF2 library. We made this for supporting multiclass devices like CDC+MSC, but that is an other story. STM32F2xx Standard Peripherals Library Drivers V1.1.2 STM32CubeF2 STM32F2xx HAL Drivers V1.1.1 STM32 USB Host Library V3.2.2 Best regards Hi @froha, Regarding the F2 HAL, latest version is **v1.2.4**. Regarding USB Host library, latest version supported in F2 firmware is **v3.3.3**. Would you mind migrating to these and check whether the issue still persists? May I also know which source file the couple of lines of code you put in your first comment are extracted from. It would help us very much to locate and fix the issue if confirmed. Thank you, Hi @ALABSTM, no, because the flag is not handled in the source code, so it wouldn't solve the problem. We fixed it ourselves and made other changes. And i cannot reproduce a Babble Error now to verify. The line of codes are from the STM32CubeF4 / Drivers / STM32F4xx_HAL_Driver
